title: rape-sentencing-guideline.pdf — section 12
text:
27. In assessing the periods under paragraphs 23(i) and (ii), 24, and 25, the court should have
regard to paragraphs 10 -12 and 16 - 20.

28. This should still not take into account any period of imprisonment or detention which may be
necessary for the protection of the public.7
Notification requirements (‘the register’)

29. The imposition of any sentence for the offences to which this guideline applies will
automatically result in the offender being made the subject of the notification requirements of
the Sexual Offences Act 2003. (These requirements are sometimes referred to as a ‘register’.)
The period for which the notification requirements apply to the offender depends on the
sentence imposed.
Non-harassment orders
Offence aggravated by domestic abuse

30. Where the offence is one to which the aggravation in section 1(1)(a) of the Abusive Behaviour
and Sexual Harm (Scotland) Act 2016 applies (offence aggravated by involving abuse of the
partner or ex-partner of the person committing it), the court must make a non-harassment order
(NHO) unless it concludes that there is no need for any of the following people to be protected
from harassment or further harassment:
• the victim
